connection.title: How is the boiler connected?
connection.description:
How Home Assistant reaches the boiler. These answers switch nothing on. If Home Assistant stops:

- **OpenTherm Gateway** and **OTGW firmware over MQTT** — the gateway drops the setpoint within a minute: a thermostat on it takes over, else heating stops.
- **ESPHome OpenTherm** — keeps its last values until it restarts, then its start values.
- **EMS-ESP** — the setpoint lapses within a minute: the boiler's own setting.
- **Relay** — stays as it was.
- **Wi-Fi module or manufacturer's integration** — monitoring by default.
- **Another writable entity** — up to the device.
- **Read only** — the plugin only reads.

data_description.connection: How Home Assistant reaches the boiler; required. It decides the write path and what the boiler does when Home Assistant stops. A wrong answer offers a path the boiler cannot take.
data_description.heat_source: Gas, oil, electric or other; required. It decides which fields and alarms apply: an electric boiler has no flame, flue gas or condensing.
data_description.type: Heating only or combi, each with or without a tank; required. It tells hot-water runs from heating: a wrong type counts one as the other.

mode.title: Control mode
mode.description: What the plugin does with the boiler. Full control sets the water temperature and switches heating; on/off switches heating only; monitoring only writes nothing. Choosing switches nothing on: control has its own switch, off until you turn it on.

data_description.control_mode: No default: chosen on purpose. Only the modes the connection can do are offered.
data_description.condensing: Condensing boilers get condensing flue-gas limits and are judged on how often they condense. A wrong answer warns late or for nothing, and skews the verdict.
data_description.dhw_priority: On (default): during hot water the rooms get no heat — a combi, or a tank on a three-way valve. Off: both run together. A wrong answer pauses the zones' learning needlessly, or lets them learn without heat.

interface.title: Boiler interface
interface.description: What the plugin needs to know about the device between it and the boiler: its MQTT topics, the gateway, how it sits between thermostat and boiler, and its restart indicator. Only what your connection and control mode use is asked.

data.thermostat_kind: What is wired to the gateway's thermostat terminals

data_description.mqtt_top: The firmware's MQTT top topic (OTGW by default): its values come under top/value/node/, the plugin's commands go to top/set/node/. The gateway keeps heating on/off; the plugin sends it again with the control setpoint, every 30 s.
data_description.mqtt_node: The firmware's node or unique ID from its MQTT settings. A wrong one: the plugin hears nothing, and its commands go nowhere.
data_description.ems_esp_base: EMS-ESP's MQTT base (ems-esp by default); its boiler data come under base/boiler_data. Published on change only, its values are judged by Home Assistant's reports alone.
data_description.gateway_id: The gateway on this boiler, as set up in the OpenTherm Gateway integration; only enabled ones are offered — another one would get the plugin's commands, and this boiler none. The gateway keeps heating on/off; the plugin sends it again with the control setpoint, every 30 s.
data_description.topology: How the gateway sits between thermostat and boiler, as it is. With a thermostat: on hand-back it takes over; while the plugin controls, its heating setting does nothing. Stand-alone: on hand-back, or when Home Assistant stops for over a minute, heating stops. Virtual: a controller on Home Assistant's side (ESPHome, EMS-ESP). After a hand-back the water follows the boiler's or thermostat's own maximum, not the plugin's.
data_description.thermostat_kind: What is on the gateway's thermostat terminals: an OpenTherm thermostat, or nothing (stand-alone). An on/off contact or "I don't know": control is not offered — after a Home Assistant crash the plugin's "heating off" would block that thermostat.
data_description.thermostat_setpoint_entity: Optional, with an OpenTherm thermostat: the water temperature the thermostat asks for (its device's "Control setpoint 1"). It tells the thermostat's request from another controller, and confirms a hand-back to it — over MQTT none is confirmed without it.
data_description.restart_entity: Optional: a sensor that shows the device's restarts — an uptime, a restart counter or a boot time. After a restart the boiler falling back to its own value is sent again, not taken for another controller.

name.title: Smart Boiler for Versatile Thermostat
name.description: Pick a name and the level of detail. The plugin monitors your boiler; it writes nothing to the boiler until you switch control on.

data_description.name: Shown as the device name.
data_description.level: Simple shows the essentials with cautious defaults; advanced shows every parameter. The level changes only what you see, never how the plugin behaves.

menu.title: Smart Boiler for Versatile Thermostat
menu.description: Go through each section: once confirmed it returns here, and nothing is created until you choose “Create”. Closing this window discards the setup. {state}

signals.title: Boiler signals
signals.description:
Pick the entity for each signal. None is required: flame and flow enable the burner's metrics, the boiler link and control of the water temperature; each other signal adds to the monitor. The plugin only reads them; one entity feeds one signal.

{hint}

data.relay_reads_boiler: Do you also read the boiler through another integration?
data.boiler_lockout: Boiler lockout (a fault that stops the boiler)

data_description.relay_reads_boiler: No (default): only what a relay setup reads is asked — flame, flow, return, the boiler's power, gas, outdoor, weather; other signals go at the save. Yes: every boiler signal, shown once you submit.
data_description.flame: On while the burner burns. Every burner-cycle metric comes from it: the wrong entity gives wrong starts and burn times.
data_description.flow: Water leaving the boiler. It tells whether heat reaches the zones and hot water from heating; with control, part of the boiler link.
data_description.return: Water coming back to the boiler. It gives the condensing share and tells, against the flow, whether heat reaches the zones.
data_description.modulation: Burner modulation in percent. With the boiler's power range it estimates heat output and gas use. A sensor in another unit is refused.
data_description.dhw_active: On while the boiler heats hot water. Without it hot-water runs are guessed, and some may count as heating.
data_description.pressure: Enables the high-pressure and "add water" alerts and the falling-pressure warning. From an OpenTherm Gateway, 0 bar counts as unknown: it shows 0 after a restart.
data_description.outdoor: Any outdoor temperature sensor, for degree-days and the curve. Checked against the weather entity: one stuck or far off is left out of the curve.
data_description.ch_setpoint: The flow setpoint the boiler received, e.g. the gateway's "Control setpoint 1" on its boiler device. Required for water-temperature control: each write is checked against it. The entity you write, or EMS-ESP's selflowtemp, shows the setpoint as unverified.
data_description.ch_enabled: Optional: whether the boiler receives heating on, e.g. the gateway's "Central heating 1" reading On/Off — not Running. With it, heating on/off is checked like the setpoint; without it, unverified. Pick one that reports a change within about a minute: a slower one delays noticing a change, and one slower than 5 min can make the plugin wrongly step aside.
data_description.ch_active: On while the boiler heats the rooms. Helps tell DHW from heating when there is no DHW signal.
data_description.pump_running: On while the heating pump runs. Enables the low-flow warning: every valve closed while the pump runs.
data_description.flue_gas: Enables the flue gas alarm and the early warning of a fouling heat exchanger.
data_description.gas_meter: A cumulative gas or energy meter: measured gas per degree-day instead of an estimate. Gas used while the burner is off is shown apart; what other appliances use while it runs counts as heating.
data_description.room_setpoint: The setpoint of a thermostat wired to the boiler or its interface, from the thermostat's side (e.g. "Room setpoint 1" on the gateway's thermostat device). Shown as what it keeps after a hand-back.
data_description.room_temperature: The room temperature a thermostat connected to the boiler or its interface sends to the boiler, if there is one. Recorded for the assessment.
data_description.weather: Its forecasts are recorded for later features; its temperature stands in for a missing or suspect outdoor sensor. No data leaves Home Assistant.
data_description.boiler_power: Optional: the boiler's electric power, e.g. from a plug that measures it; used only as proof that a relay-driven boiler heats.
data_description.low_pressure_fault: Optional: the boiler's own low-water-pressure fault (e.g. the gateway's "Low water pressure"). On for 5 minutes: control switches heating off, without a hand-back, until it clears. A wrong pick stops heating needlessly. On a gateway it counts only with the fault indication on.
data_description.boiler_lockout: Optional: a fault your boiler's manual says stops it (a lockout), not a service flag. On for 5 minutes: control switches heating off, without a hand-back, until it clears. EMS-ESP needs a template sensor from its service codes. On a gateway a detail counts only with the fault indication on.
data_description.fault_indication: Optional: the boiler's general fault indication (e.g. the gateway's "Fault indication"). It stops nothing itself. On an OpenTherm Gateway the two faults above count only while it is on: the gateway never clears their details.

boiler.title: Boiler
boiler.description: What you know about the boiler; leave unknown values empty — the plugin then says what it cannot judge. A field shows only where its signal is mapped; a value already set stays, hidden.

data_description.boiler_min_power: Lowest heating power from the manual, in kW. A building load often below it means the boiler must cycle; a wrong value skews the verdict.
data_description.boiler_max_power: Highest heating power in kW. With the minimum and the modulation it estimates heat output; a wrong value skews heat and gas estimates.
data_description.max_ch_setpoint: Highest flow temperature in heating, in °C. Flow above it points to hot water, and control never writes above it. Too low: heating counts as hot water, and rooms stay cold in hard frost.
data_description.gas_at_min_power: Gas per hour at minimum power, from the manual's technical data: m³/h (kg/h for LPG). With the modulation it estimates gas use without a gas meter.
data_description.gas_at_max_power: Gas per hour at maximum power, from the same technical data and in the same unit; a wrong value skews the gas estimates.
data_description.modulation_scale: Whether 0 % is the minimum power (the OpenTherm definition) or the value is a percentage of maximum power. The wrong choice skews heat and gas estimates.
data_description.bypass: Tick with an automatic bypass valve or a low-loss header: closed valves cannot stop the flow, so the low-flow warning is off. A wrong tick gives false warnings, or leaves a real dead-end unwarned.
data_description.add_water_below: Optional: below this pressure, in bar, you are told to add water — the boiler's minimum operating pressure from its manual. Empty by default: no notification. It only informs.
data_description.pressure_high_warning: Optional: a warning above this pressure, in bar; empty (default): none. Keep it below the safety valve's rating (on the valve; often 3 bar in Europe) and below the alarm. It only informs.
data_description.pressure_high_alarm: Optional: an alarm above this pressure, in bar, and a notification after 5 minutes; empty (default): none. Below the safety valve's rating, read on the valve (often 3 bar in Europe), above the warning. Too high tells you only after the valve has let water out.

circuit.title: Heating circuit: {name}
circuit.description: How this circuit's water temperature is set.

data_description.name: Shown in the menu. Pick a Home Assistant area or a VT zone, or type any name; the plugin's own ID stays hidden. Empty: the circuit's number.
data_description.control: Straight from the boiler (unmixed); mixed by the boiler (a second circuit); controlled by other automation (a mixer or pump the plugin never drives); or a thermostatic mixing valve (fixed). Control runs with at most one straight circuit and none the boiler mixes.
data_description.zones: The Versatile Thermostat zones this circuit heats. A zone in no circuit neither asks for heat nor is watched for frost; a zone is in one circuit unless split by its devices. One built on the boiler's own thermostat is refused: it would ask whenever the flame burns.
data_description.area: A shortcut: the VT zones in this Home Assistant area are added to the list at the save.
data_description.devices: Optional: for a room this circuit feeds only in part — a radiator here, a floor loop on another circuit — its own devices instead of the whole zone. In a circuit run by other automation it then asks only while one of them is on.
data_description.underfloor: This circuit's zones with underfloor heating: their curve exponent and the circuit's highest water temperature apply. The rest are radiators unless convectors.
data_description.convectors: The zones of this circuit with convectors (fan coils). The rest are radiators unless listed as underfloor.
data_description.max_flow: The most this circuit may receive, in °C (70 where empty); with control no setpoint goes above it. Needed for unmixed underfloor. Too high overheats emitters or a floor; too low: rooms stay cold in frost. After a hand-back the boiler's or thermostat's own maximum is the only one.
data_description.fixed_temperature: A thermostatic mixing valve's setting, in °C; required for that type. The boiler's water stays at least 5 K above it, so the valve can reach it.
data_description.request_entity: Optional: an entity on while the circuit's own controller (a mixer, a pump) wants heat; the boiler heats for it as for a zone. Unreadable, it asks nothing and the control state says so.
data_description.needed_temperature: Optional: while the circuit asks, the boiler's water stays at or above this plus 5 K — the margin its mixer mixes down from. Empty, the curve gives the water.
data_description.needed_entity: Optional: an entity reporting the water the circuit needs now, taken before the value above; unreadable, the value is used.
data_description.max_flow_alarm: Information alarm when the measured flow stays above this, in °C. Starts at the maximum + 5 °C. Needs a flow reading. Too high lets a real overshoot pass unreported.
data_description.max_flow_alarm_min: How long, in minutes, before the alarm rises. Starts at 10. Too short reports every overshoot of the boiler's hysteresis.
data_description.flow_entity: A mixed circuit's own flow temperature. Without it the heat reaching that circuit cannot be told.
data_description.remove_circuit: Removes the circuit at the save, and its zones with it: they are no longer watched. Not offered for the only one.

zones.title: VT zones
zones.description: The Versatile Thermostat zones the circuits feed: {zones}. They are picked in each circuit's form; a zone in no circuit is neither watched nor asked for heat.

data.closes_when_off: Valves close when the zone is off

data_description.closes_when_off: Zones whose valves close while VT has them off, where VT does not publish the valve state. Off unless ticked: a wrong tick lets the plugin take a closed zone for an open one.

building.title: Building
building.description: What the monitor knows of the house's heat loss, for its statistics. Recorded days measure it; a value you enter always wins — the data never replace it, they only show a mismatch. Nothing here switches heating.

data.design_outdoor: Outdoor temperature at the hardest frost

data_description.design_load_kw: Your own heat-loss calculation, in kW at the hardest frost. Always wins: recorded days never replace it, they only show a mismatch. A value no house has is refused.
data_description.heating_threshold: Outdoor temperature above which the house needs no heating, in °C: the base of degree-days. It switches no heating. Default 15 °C until recorded days measure it; entered, it wins.
data_description.design_outdoor: The outdoor temperature your design load is given for, in °C: the frost of a few days a year. Default −15 °C. Wrong, the heat loss read from the design load is skewed.

monitor.title: Monitor
monitor.description: Thresholds of the analysis; each shows only where its signal is mapped. A value already set stays, hidden.

data.monitoring_days: Days of data for the verdict

data_description.condensing_return: A return below this counts as condensing, in °C. Default 55 °C. Too high overstates the condensing share.
data_description.short_burn_min: Burns shorter than this count as short, in minutes. Default 10. Longer makes more burns short, and the verdict harsher.
data_description.monitoring_days: Days of data the monitor's verdict needs, from when the integration was added. Default 7, the shortest. It holds nothing back: control can be switched on any time, even without a verdict; until then the switch shows "not enough data".
data_description.flue_gas_warning: Flue gas above this raises a warning on a condensing boiler, in °C. Default 85 °C. Too high warns too late.
data_description.flue_gas_alarm: Flue gas above this raises an alarm, in °C. Default 100 °C. A limit set too high warns too late for plastic flue pipes.
data_description.starts_per_hour_limit: More burner starts than this in an hour raise a warning. Default 12. Too high hides short-cycling.
data_description.unstable_burns_limit: More than this many burns under a minute in a day raise a warning. Default 10. Too high hides an ignition problem.
data_description.verdict_window_days: The verdict covers this many most recent days with data. Empty (default): every day kept, up to a year, filled from the recorder at start. Never shorter than the monitoring period.

control.title: Control (experimental)
control.description: How the plugin writes to the boiler: a flow setpoint, or on and off through a relay. Until you switch control on, nothing changes; you may switch it on from the first day, even without a verdict. It then replaces VT's central boiler — remove that first and restart Home Assistant. The boiler's connection decides the path.

data_description.write_path: Asked only for an installation set up before the connection question: no control (default), a writable entity (e.g. EMS-ESP, ESPHome), the OpenTherm Gateway integration, the OTGW firmware's MQTT, or a relay for an on/off boiler. A wrong path: writes that fail or go nowhere.

control_entity.title: Writable entity
control_entity.description: The entity that takes the flow setpoint, and how control is handed back.

data.own_room_controller: The boiler has its own room controller
data.esphome_safe_start: On the ESP: safe start values and a short API reboot_timeout

data_description.setpoint_entity: A number or input_number that sets the boiler's flow temperature. Another value — the boiler's maximum, a hot-water setting — would be overwritten every 30 s or 5 min, and the water would not follow the curve.
data_description.write_type: Expiring: dropped unless repeated — repeated every 30 s. Held: the device keeps it — written on change, every 5 min and on its return; "off" included, it stays while Home Assistant is down. Persistent or unknown (default): not available — the plugin never writes to the boiler's memory, which every repeat would wear.
data_description.ch_entity: A switch that turns heating on and off — needed for control in this version: without it "off" would be a low setpoint. Turned back on at hand-back where the boiler or a thermostat takes over. Never a setting stored in the boiler's memory, nor a flag that stops heating while on (EMS-ESP's "heating off").
data_description.ch_write_type: What the device does with the switch's state. Expiring: repeated every 30 s. Held: written on change, every 5 min and on its return. Persistent or unknown: refused — the plugin never writes to the boiler's memory.
data_description.hand_back: How control returns to the boiler on every exit, after the lowest water temperature is written and the heating switch turned back on where the boiler takes over: write a value, let the device's timeout lapse (expiring writes only), or turn off an external-control switch. Required. Afterwards the boiler's or thermostat's own maximum is the only one.
data_description.hand_back_value: The setpoint written on hand-back, in °C. 0 means "own control" on some devices and "no heat" on others. Never above the highest water temperature, and never cut down to it; done once the read-back shows it.
data_description.hand_back_value_effect: What the device does with that value: its own control resumes, or heating stops. Declared "own control" where heating stops, a hand-back leaves the house unheated while the plugin says the boiler runs on its own.
data_description.hand_back_entity: The switch that enables external control: on when control starts, off on hand-back — so never a setting the device stores in its memory.
data_description.hand_back_entity_write_type: What the device does with the switch's state. Expiring: turned on again every 30 s while control holds the boiler. Held: on when control takes the boiler, every 5 min and on its return. Persistent or unknown (default): not available — every switching would wear the boiler's memory.
data_description.hand_back_timeout_min: How long, in minutes, the device keeps the last value before its own control resumes — from its documentation (1–60; default 1, as EMS-ESP's setpoint). The boiler stays at the lowest water temperature that long; the hand-back is judged after it. Too short: a false alarm; too long: a device that never lets go is reported late.
data_description.own_room_controller: Tick only if the boiler has its own room controller that asks for heat once the plugin lets go (e.g. a room unit on its EMS bus). Hand-backs then go to it, also when VT gives no answer at all. Off by default. Without such a controller, the boiler would heat on its own dial with no room in charge.
data_description.esphome_safe_start: Required for control on ESPHome; never ticked for you. The ESP keeps the last setpoint and heating until it restarts (by default after 15 min without Home Assistant), then takes its start values. Tick once those are safe unattended, restore_value is off and its reboot_timeout is a few minutes.

control_relay.title: Relay
control_relay.description: How the plugin switches an on/off boiler, as VT's central boiler did; the boiler sets its own water temperature, so the curve and water limits do not apply. If Home Assistant stops, the relay stays as it was: switch it by hand in the relay's own app or web page. A relay in the boiler's power supply also cuts its pump overrun and frost protection; the room-thermostat terminals may carry mains voltage.

data.relay_is_separate_contact: This relay or thermostat entity is not a setting stored in the boiler's memory
data.relay_reports_state: The relay reports its real state
data.own_room_controller: The boiler has its own room controller

data_description.relay_entity: The switch on the boiler's room-thermostat terminals, or a boiler thermostat entity set to heat or off. Not a helper, not a VT zone's switch, never a setting stored in the boiler's memory. A Zigbee relay may look available long after it dies: turn availability reporting on.
data_description.relay_is_separate_contact: Tick to confirm the relay is a separate contact — or, for a boiler thermostat entity, that its heat/off mode is not stored in the boiler's memory, which every switching would wear (e.g. EMS-ESP's "heating activated"). Unsure: leave it unticked. Control does not start without it.
data_description.relay_reports_state: Yes: the plugin checks the relay's state, writes only when it differs, and steps aside if something else keeps switching it. No or I don't know (default): it repeats its command at the repeat interval, unconfirmed; a change made at the relay is undone within that time.
data_description.relay_power_on_state: What the relay does when its power returns — its own setting. Off: the boiler waits until Home Assistant gives its command. On, last state or I don't know (default): after a power cut the boiler may heat without control until Home Assistant is back.
data_description.relay_off_timer: Whether the relay switches itself off some time after "on" (Tasmota's PulseTime; a Shelly's auto-off — whether a Shelly restarts it on a repeated "on" is not documented). None: written only on a difference. A length: "on" repeated at half of it; if Home Assistant stops, the relay switches heating off by itself. I don't know (default): "on" repeated at the repeat interval; switch-offs coming the same time after "on", 9 min or more (a 10-min timer measured up to a minute short), are taken for its timer, other ones count, and the fourth within a day makes the plugin step aside — so declare its length. Set a relay timer only once the plugin's control starts.
data_description.relay_off_timer_min: The timer's length, 10–120 min, exactly as set in the relay: a switch-off at another time counts as something else switching the relay. A shorter timer is refused: each lapse would start the boiler again.
data_description.relay_repeat_s: How often the command is repeated, in seconds, 10–300; empty (default): 300 s, or VT's keep-alive where it was at most 300 s. A relay that restarted in the wrong state stays so at most this long; some relays store every command.
data_description.relay_rest_state: What the relay is set to whenever control is handed back. Off (default): without a thermostat wired to the boiler heating stops, and the plugin tells you when a room asks for heat or nears freezing. On: the boiler heats by its own setting, rooms limited only by their valves.
data_description.own_room_controller: Tick only if the boiler has its own room controller and the relay after hand-back is "on": when VT gives no answer, the relay goes on and that controller heats. With "off" the tick changes nothing. Off by default.
data_description.boiler_heats_above_w: The boiler's electric power, in W, above which it counts as heating. Empty (default): power is not used as proof. Too low: standby counts as heating; too high: real heating is missed.

control_relay_from_vt.title: Relay — moving over from Versatile Thermostat
control_relay_from_vt.description: How the plugin switches an on/off boiler, as VT's central boiler did; the boiler sets its own water temperature, so the curve and water limits do not apply. If Home Assistant stops, the relay stays as it was: switch it by hand in the relay's own app or web page. A relay in the boiler's power supply also cuts its pump overrun and frost protection; the room-thermostat terminals may carry mains voltage. VT's central boiler drives this boiler now: its relay, delay, repeat interval and thresholds are filled in where usable — check and save. Then untick "Use a central boiler" in VT, restart Home Assistant, untick "Used by central boiler" in rooms where Auto-TPI learns, move automations off VT's boiler sensor, and switch control on.

data.relay_reports_state: The relay reports its real state
data.own_room_controller: The boiler has its own room controller

On: the boiler heats by its own setting, rooms limited only by their valves.

control_curve.title: Heating curve
control_curve.description: The flow temperature the house needs at each outdoor temperature, the lowest water temperature and the comfort correction. The water is capped by the highest water temperature of the circuits fed straight from the boiler ({circuit_max}, the circuits' forms; 70 °C where none) and the boiler's maximum heating setpoint ({boiler_max}, boiler step): the lower applies.

data.design_outdoor: Outdoor temperature at the hardest frost (curve point)

data_description.design_outdoor: The curve's design point, in °C: at this outdoor temperature the water is at the design flow temperature. Default −15 °C. Too cold a value gives too little water in frost.
data_description.design_flow: The flow temperature the heating needs at the hardest frost, in °C (e.g. from the boiler's own curve). Required, no default. Too high wastes gas and makes the burner cycle; too low leaves rooms cold. SmartPI (0.4.0) learns its own outdoor term in each zone: set the curve to what the house needs, no higher.
data_description.hard_min: The lowest water temperature the plugin sets, in °C. Default 20 °C. Too low: in mild weather the boiler stops again and again, and a non-condensing boiler condenses in its flue — take it from the manual. The plugin may suggest a value; it never changes this itself.
data_description.room: With Manual: the setpoint of the warmest room you keep, in °C. Default 20 °C. Too low leaves rooms cold in mild weather; too high raises the whole curve. With Auto, the start value until a zone is known.
data_description.exponent: How the curve bends. Empty picks it from the emitters: radiators 1.3, convectors 1.4, underfloor 1.1. The wrong bend under-heats in frost or overheats in mild weather.
data_description.offset: Shifts the whole curve up or down, in K. Default 0. Up wastes gas; down leaves rooms cold.
data_description.fallback_setpoint: Used when no outdoor temperature has been known for three hours (sensor and weather lost or suspect), in °C. Empty (default): the curve at its design point, the most heat it gives; the valves keep rooms from overheating.
data_description.comfort_correction: On (default with full control): while a zone's valve is fully open and its room stays short of its setpoint (with SmartPI learning: of the setpoint + 0.5 K), the water rises above the curve — 1 K per 30 min, at most 3 K a day, up to its limit — and falls twice as fast; not while another zone is too warm or the starts rise. What it costs: more gas, and possibly more starts. With TPI zones it can sit at its limit: in the simulation 1.75 to 5 times the starts. Watch the starts.
data_description.room_mode: Auto (default): the curve passes through the highest setpoint among the zones that heat now — at most 23 °C, following VT's presets. Manual: the value below. With Auto the warmest room sets the water for all; a room kept warm only now and then raises it too, unless left out below.
data_description.room_excluded: Zones whose setpoint Auto does not follow, e.g. a bathroom kept warmer. Such a room may stay short in mild weather; the comfort correction then raises the water for it.
data_description.comfort_correction_max_k: How far above the curve the correction may raise the water, in K. Default 3 K, 0.5 to 10; it rises at most 3 K a day. It is the only bound above the curve. Higher: more gas and warmer water for rooms that do not need it; a correction stuck at its limit means the curve is too low.

control_behaviour.title: Control behaviour
control_behaviour.description: Heating goes on and off with VT's zones, at once — after the activation delay for a start; nothing counted or timed holds it. At the advanced level: the demand thresholds and learning pauses; with full control the ramp, the decision interval and, without a heating switch, the "off" setpoint.

data_description.activation_delay_s: Seconds heating waits after the first call for heat, so slow valves open before the boiler and pump run, as VT's central boiler did; pre-filled from VT's own, for you to confirm. Stopping is never delayed. Default 0. A heating pulse shorter than the delay never starts the boiler.
data_description.ramp_k_per_min: The fastest setpoint change, in K per minute. Default 1. Faster changes stress the boiler and make zones overshoot.
data_description.decision_interval_min: How often the water temperature is decided anew, in minutes; default 5. Heating on and off follows the zones every 10 s regardless. Shorter follows the weather sooner but moves the water more often under the zones' algorithms.
data_description.off_setpoint: The setpoint written for "off" without a heating switch, in °C. Default 10, below the lowest water temperature. A low setpoint may not switch the boiler's heating off — the pump may keep running. Control without a heating switch is blocked in this version, so it is not written yet.
data_description.count_threshold: Heating is needed when at least this many zones call. Default 1, at most the number of zones. 0 leaves the power or opening threshold alone — every zone must then report what it needs, or it could never ask for heat. Higher leaves a single room without heat.
data_description.power_threshold_kw: Optional: heating is needed when the zones' mean power, as VT counts it, reaches this, in kW, while a valve is open or a device on. A zone without a device power in VT gives no data. Too high leaves small rooms without heat.
data_description.opening_threshold: Optional: heating is needed when the widest valve opening among the calling zones reaches this, in %. VT's over_climate zones give no data. Too high leaves a room that opens a little without heat.
data_description.learning_pauses: Pause SmartPI's learning while hot water runs, while control holds heating off for a boiler fault and while the water swings, so it does not learn what the boiler did; at most an hour each. Default on. Auto-TPI cannot be paused without losing what it learned: such zones are reported.

control_frost.title: Frost protection
control_frost.description: A watched zone colder than its limit starts heating, whatever else applies, where heat can reach it; heating for frost ends once every watched zone is above the release.

data_description.frost_limit: A watched zone colder than this starts heating, whatever else applies, where heat can reach it, in °C. Default 5 °C. Too low risks frozen pipes; too high heats rooms you keep off.
data_description.frost_release: Frost protection ends once every watched zone is above this, in °C. Default 7 °C, above the limit. Close to the limit, frost heating starts and stops more often.
data_description.frost_zone: Optional: watch only this zone. Empty (default): every zone. Frost heating runs only for a cold room whose valve can open; one VT keeps closed raises a repair issue. Frost heating that does not warm the room in two hours raises an alarm; it never stops.

control_alarms.title: Alarm reactions
control_alarms.description: What control does when the boiler ignores a value the plugin writes. Other alarms only inform; the plugin stops heating only while the boiler itself reports a fault that stops it. Another controller writing to the boiler always makes the plugin step aside; it never fights it.

data.return_after_outside_change: Return by itself after another controller
data.return_after_switch_hand_back: Also after the external-control switch's hand-back

data_description.write_ignored: Offered where a hand-back returns the boiler to a thermostat or its own control. Hand back: after an ignored write, control steps aside until you switch it off and on. Information (default): the plugin keeps trying and tells you. "Heating off" ignored from the start always hands back.
data_description.return_after_outside_change: Off (default): after another controller changed the boiler twice, the plugin hands back and steps aside until you switch control off and on. On: it takes the boiler back after an hour with no other writes. If the other controller only pauses, the two take turns.
data_description.return_after_switch_hand_back: Used only with the return above on. Off (default): after a hand-back through the external-control switch, control waits for you. On: it returns once the switch has read "off" for an hour — also when a person turned external control off on purpose.

control_return_confirm.title: Confirm the return by itself
control_return_confirm.description: The plugin will take the boiler back by itself an hour after another controller last wrote to it. If that controller is still there, both will control the boiler in turns. Tick to confirm.

data_description.understood: Tick to switch the return by itself on; without the tick it stays off.

init.title: Smart Boiler for Versatile Thermostat options
init.description:
{changes}

Each section returns here once confirmed; nothing is saved until you choose “Save and finish”, which checks everything, saves it and reloads the integration once: while control holds the boiler, it is handed back and taken again (a relay goes to its rest state and back). Changing only the level reloads nothing. Closing this window discards the unsaved changes.

menu_options.level_hidden: Level of detail (some hidden advanced settings are active)

connection.title: How is the boiler connected?
connection.description:
How Home Assistant reaches the boiler. These answers switch nothing on. If Home Assistant stops:

- **OpenTherm Gateway** and **OTGW firmware over MQTT** — the gateway drops the setpoint within a minute: a thermostat on it takes over, else heating stops.
- **ESPHome OpenTherm** — keeps its last values until it restarts, then its start values.
- **EMS-ESP** — the setpoint lapses within a minute: the boiler's own setting.
- **Relay** — stays as it was.
- **Wi-Fi module or manufacturer's integration** — monitoring by default.
- **Another writable entity** — up to the device.
- **Read only** — the plugin only reads.

data_description.connection: How Home Assistant reaches the boiler; required. It decides the write path and what the boiler does when Home Assistant stops. A wrong answer offers a path the boiler cannot take.
data_description.heat_source: Gas, oil, electric or other; required. It decides which fields and alarms apply: an electric boiler has no flame, flue gas or condensing.
data_description.type: Heating only or combi, each with or without a tank; required. It tells hot-water runs from heating: a wrong type counts one as the other.

mode.title: Control mode
mode.description: What the plugin does with the boiler. Full control sets the water temperature and switches heating; on/off switches heating only; monitoring only writes nothing. Choosing switches nothing on: control has its own switch, off until you turn it on.

data_description.control_mode: No default: chosen on purpose. Only the modes the connection can do are offered.
data_description.condensing: Condensing boilers get condensing flue-gas limits and are judged on how often they condense. A wrong answer warns late or for nothing, and skews the verdict.
data_description.dhw_priority: On (default): during hot water the rooms get no heat — a combi, or a tank on a three-way valve. Off: both run together. A wrong answer pauses the zones' learning needlessly, or lets them learn without heat.

interface.title: Boiler interface
interface.description: What the plugin needs to know about the device between it and the boiler: its MQTT topics, the gateway, how it sits between thermostat and boiler, and its restart indicator. Only what your connection and control mode use is asked.

data.thermostat_kind: What is wired to the gateway's thermostat terminals

data_description.mqtt_top: The firmware's MQTT top topic (OTGW by default): its values come under top/value/node/, the plugin's commands go to top/set/node/. The gateway keeps heating on/off; the plugin sends it again with the control setpoint, every 30 s.
data_description.mqtt_node: The firmware's node or unique ID from its MQTT settings. A wrong one: the plugin hears nothing, and its commands go nowhere.
data_description.ems_esp_base: EMS-ESP's MQTT base (ems-esp by default); its boiler data come under base/boiler_data. Published on change only, its values are judged by Home Assistant's reports alone.
data_description.gateway_id: The gateway on this boiler, as set up in the OpenTherm Gateway integration; only enabled ones are offered — another one would get the plugin's commands, and this boiler none. The gateway keeps heating on/off; the plugin sends it again with the control setpoint, every 30 s.
data_description.topology: How the gateway sits between thermostat and boiler, as it is. With a thermostat: on hand-back it takes over; while the plugin controls, its heating setting does nothing. Stand-alone: on hand-back, or when Home Assistant stops for over a minute, heating stops. Virtual: a controller on Home Assistant's side (ESPHome, EMS-ESP). After a hand-back the water follows the boiler's or thermostat's own maximum, not the plugin's.
data_description.thermostat_kind: What is on the gateway's thermostat terminals: an OpenTherm thermostat, or nothing (stand-alone). An on/off contact or "I don't know": control is not offered — after a Home Assistant crash the plugin's "heating off" would block that thermostat.
data_description.thermostat_setpoint_entity: Optional, with an OpenTherm thermostat: the water temperature the thermostat asks for (its device's "Control setpoint 1"). It tells the thermostat's request from another controller, and confirms a hand-back to it — over MQTT none is confirmed without it.
data_description.restart_entity: Optional: a sensor that shows the device's restarts — an uptime, a restart counter or a boot time. After a restart the boiler falling back to its own value is sent again, not taken for another controller.

level.title: Level of detail
level.description: The level changes only what you see, never how the plugin behaves: switching it alone reloads nothing at “Save and finish”; restoring the defaults reloads the integration.

data.restore_defaults: Restore advanced settings to their defaults

data_description.level: Simple shows the essentials; advanced shows every parameter.
data_description.restore_defaults: When switching to simple: tick to reset the advanced tuning — control's curve shape and behaviour, the alarm reactions, the monitor's thresholds — to its defaults. Facts about the installation stay. Unticked, the tuning stays active but hidden.

signals.title: Boiler signals
signals.description:
Pick the entity for each signal. None is required: flame and flow enable the burner's metrics, the boiler link and control of the water temperature; each other signal adds to the monitor. The plugin only reads them; one entity feeds one signal.

{hint}

data.relay_reads_boiler: Do you also read the boiler through another integration?
data.boiler_lockout: Boiler lockout (a fault that stops the boiler)

data_description.relay_reads_boiler: No (default): only what a relay setup reads is asked — flame, flow, return, the boiler's power, gas, outdoor, weather; other signals go at the save. Yes: every boiler signal, shown once you submit.
data_description.flame: On while the burner burns. Every burner-cycle metric comes from it: the wrong entity gives wrong starts and burn times.
data_description.flow: Water leaving the boiler. It tells whether heat reaches the zones and hot water from heating; with control, part of the boiler link.
data_description.return: Water coming back to the boiler. It gives the condensing share and tells, against the flow, whether heat reaches the zones.
data_description.modulation: Burner modulation in percent. With the boiler's power range it estimates heat output and gas use. A sensor in another unit is refused.
data_description.dhw_active: On while the boiler heats hot water. Without it hot-water runs are guessed, and some may count as heating.
data_description.pressure: Enables the high-pressure and "add water" alerts and the falling-pressure warning. From an OpenTherm Gateway, 0 bar counts as unknown: it shows 0 after a restart.
data_description.outdoor: Any outdoor temperature sensor, for degree-days and the curve. Checked against the weather entity: one stuck or far off is left out of the curve.
data_description.ch_setpoint: The flow setpoint the boiler received, e.g. the gateway's "Control setpoint 1" on its boiler device. Required for water-temperature control: each write is checked against it. The entity you write, or EMS-ESP's selflowtemp, shows the setpoint as unverified.
data_description.ch_enabled: Optional: whether the boiler receives heating on, e.g. the gateway's "Central heating 1" reading On/Off — not Running. With it, heating on/off is checked like the setpoint; without it, unverified. Pick one that reports a change within about a minute: a slower one delays noticing a change, and one slower than 5 min can make the plugin wrongly step aside.
data_description.ch_active: On while the boiler heats the rooms. Helps tell DHW from heating when there is no DHW signal.
data_description.pump_running: On while the heating pump runs. Enables the low-flow warning: every valve closed while the pump runs.
data_description.flue_gas: Enables the flue gas alarm and the early warning of a fouling heat exchanger.
data_description.gas_meter: A cumulative gas or energy meter: measured gas per degree-day instead of an estimate. Gas used while the burner is off is shown apart; what other appliances use while it runs counts as heating.
data_description.room_setpoint: The setpoint of a thermostat wired to the boiler or its interface, from the thermostat's side (e.g. "Room setpoint 1" on the gateway's thermostat device). Shown as what it keeps after a hand-back.
data_description.room_temperature: The room temperature a thermostat connected to the boiler or its interface sends to the boiler, if there is one. Recorded for the assessment.
data_description.weather: Its forecasts are recorded for later features; its temperature stands in for a missing or suspect outdoor sensor. No data leaves Home Assistant.
data_description.boiler_power: Optional: the boiler's electric power, e.g. from a plug that measures it; used only as proof that a relay-driven boiler heats.
data_description.low_pressure_fault: Optional: the boiler's own low-water-pressure fault (e.g. the gateway's "Low water pressure"). On for 5 minutes: control switches heating off, without a hand-back, until it clears. A wrong pick stops heating needlessly. On a gateway it counts only with the fault indication on.
data_description.boiler_lockout: Optional: a fault your boiler's manual says stops it (a lockout), not a service flag. On for 5 minutes: control switches heating off, without a hand-back, until it clears. EMS-ESP needs a template sensor from its service codes. On a gateway a detail counts only with the fault indication on.
data_description.fault_indication: Optional: the boiler's general fault indication (e.g. the gateway's "Fault indication"). It stops nothing itself. On an OpenTherm Gateway the two faults above count only while it is on: the gateway never clears their details.

freshness.title: Freshness limits
freshness.description: An age limit per signal, in minutes: a value not reported for longer counts as stale. {judged} Empty (default): automatic — five times the source's own rhythm once it is seen repeating a value (10–30 min; the weather 3–12 h); a source that reports only changes gets none. 0: availability only. Without a limit a frozen source goes unseen; one shorter than its rhythm stops control in steady weather.

data_description.flame: Its age limit in minutes. Empty (default): automatic; 0: only availability counts. Shorter than the source's reporting interval, a steady value counts as stale. Control: stale for 5 minutes within 10, the boiler is handed back.
data_description.flow: Its age limit in minutes. Empty (default): automatic; 0: only availability counts. Shorter than the source's reporting interval, a steady value counts as stale. Control: stale for 5 minutes within 10, the boiler is handed back.
data_description.return: Its age limit in minutes. Empty (default): automatic; 0: only availability counts. Shorter than the source's reporting interval, a steady value counts as stale.
data_description.modulation: Its age limit in minutes. Empty (default): automatic; 0: only availability counts. Shorter than the source's reporting interval, a steady value counts as stale.
data_description.dhw_active: Its age limit in minutes. Empty (default): automatic; 0: only availability counts. Shorter than the source's reporting interval, a steady value counts as stale.
data_description.pressure: Its age limit in minutes. Empty (default): automatic; 0: only availability counts. Shorter than the source's reporting interval, a steady value counts as stale.
data_description.outdoor: Its age limit in minutes. Empty (default): automatic; 0: only availability counts. Shorter than the source's reporting interval, a steady value counts as stale.

boiler.title: Boiler
boiler.description: What you know about the boiler; leave unknown values empty — the plugin then says what it cannot judge. A field shows only where its signal is mapped; a value already set stays, hidden.

data_description.boiler_min_power: Lowest heating power from the manual, in kW. A building load often below it means the boiler must cycle; a wrong value skews the verdict.
data_description.boiler_max_power: Highest heating power in kW. With the minimum and the modulation it estimates heat output; a wrong value skews heat and gas estimates.
data_description.max_ch_setpoint: Highest flow temperature in heating, in °C. Flow above it points to hot water, and control never writes above it. Too low: heating counts as hot water, and rooms stay cold in hard frost.
data_description.gas_at_min_power: Gas per hour at minimum power, from the manual's technical data: m³/h (kg/h for LPG). With the modulation it estimates gas use without a gas meter.
data_description.gas_at_max_power: Gas per hour at maximum power, from the same technical data and in the same unit; a wrong value skews the gas estimates.
data_description.modulation_scale: Whether 0 % is the minimum power (the OpenTherm definition) or the value is a percentage of maximum power. The wrong choice skews heat and gas estimates.
data_description.bypass: Tick with an automatic bypass valve or a low-loss header: closed valves cannot stop the flow, so the low-flow warning is off. A wrong tick gives false warnings, or leaves a real dead-end unwarned.
data_description.add_water_below: Optional: below this pressure, in bar, you are told to add water — the boiler's minimum operating pressure from its manual. Empty by default: no notification. It only informs.
data_description.pressure_high_warning: Optional: a warning above this pressure, in bar; empty (default): none. Keep it below the safety valve's rating (on the valve; often 3 bar in Europe) and below the alarm. It only informs.
data_description.pressure_high_alarm: Optional: an alarm above this pressure, in bar, and a notification after 5 minutes; empty (default): none. Below the safety valve's rating, read on the valve (often 3 bar in Europe), above the warning. Too high tells you only after the valve has let water out.

circuit.title: Heating circuit: {name}
circuit.description: How this circuit's water temperature is set.

data_description.name: Shown in the menu. Pick a Home Assistant area or a VT zone, or type any name; the plugin's own ID stays hidden. Empty: the circuit's number.
data_description.control: Straight from the boiler (unmixed); mixed by the boiler (a second circuit); controlled by other automation (a mixer or pump the plugin never drives); or a thermostatic mixing valve (fixed). Control runs with at most one straight circuit and none the boiler mixes.
data_description.zones: The Versatile Thermostat zones this circuit heats. A zone in no circuit neither asks for heat nor is watched for frost; a zone is in one circuit unless split by its devices. One built on the boiler's own thermostat is refused: it would ask whenever the flame burns.
data_description.area: A shortcut: the VT zones in this Home Assistant area are added to the list at the save.
data_description.devices: Optional: for a room this circuit feeds only in part — a radiator here, a floor loop on another circuit — its own devices instead of the whole zone. In a circuit run by other automation it then asks only while one of them is on.
data_description.underfloor: This circuit's zones with underfloor heating: their curve exponent and the circuit's highest water temperature apply. The rest are radiators unless convectors.
data_description.convectors: The zones of this circuit with convectors (fan coils). The rest are radiators unless listed as underfloor.
data_description.max_flow: The most this circuit may receive, in °C (70 where empty); with control no setpoint goes above it. Needed for unmixed underfloor. Too high overheats emitters or a floor; too low: rooms stay cold in frost. After a hand-back the boiler's or thermostat's own maximum is the only one.
data_description.fixed_temperature: A thermostatic mixing valve's setting, in °C; required for that type. The boiler's water stays at least 5 K above it, so the valve can reach it.
data_description.request_entity: Optional: an entity on while the circuit's own controller (a mixer, a pump) wants heat; the boiler heats for it as for a zone. Unreadable, it asks nothing and the control state says so.
data_description.needed_temperature: Optional: while the circuit asks, the boiler's water stays at or above this plus 5 K — the margin its mixer mixes down from. Empty, the curve gives the water.
data_description.needed_entity: Optional: an entity reporting the water the circuit needs now, taken before the value above; unreadable, the value is used.
data_description.max_flow_alarm: Information alarm when the measured flow stays above this, in °C. Starts at the maximum + 5 °C. Needs a flow reading. Too high lets a real overshoot pass unreported.
data_description.max_flow_alarm_min: How long, in minutes, before the alarm rises. Starts at 10. Too short reports every overshoot of the boiler's hysteresis.
data_description.flow_entity: A mixed circuit's own flow temperature. Without it the heat reaching that circuit cannot be told.
data_description.remove_circuit: Removes the circuit at the save, and its zones with it: they are no longer watched. Not offered for the only one.

zones.title: VT zones
zones.description: The Versatile Thermostat zones the circuits feed: {zones}. They are picked in each circuit's form; a zone in no circuit is neither watched nor asked for heat.

data.closes_when_off: Valves close when the zone is off

data_description.closes_when_off: Zones whose valves close while VT has them off, where VT does not publish the valve state. Off unless ticked: a wrong tick lets the plugin take a closed zone for an open one.

building.title: Building
building.description: What the monitor knows of the house's heat loss, for its statistics. Recorded days measure it; a value you enter always wins — the data never replace it, they only show a mismatch. Nothing here switches heating.

data.design_outdoor: Outdoor temperature at the hardest frost

data_description.design_load_kw: Your own heat-loss calculation, in kW at the hardest frost. Always wins: recorded days never replace it, they only show a mismatch. A value no house has is refused.
data_description.heating_threshold: Outdoor temperature above which the house needs no heating, in °C: the base of degree-days. It switches no heating. Default 15 °C until recorded days measure it; entered, it wins.
data_description.design_outdoor: The outdoor temperature your design load is given for, in °C: the frost of a few days a year. Default −15 °C. Wrong, the heat loss read from the design load is skewed.

monitor.title: Monitor
monitor.description: Thresholds of the analysis; each shows only where its signal is mapped. A value already set stays, hidden.

data.monitoring_days: Days of data for the verdict

data_description.condensing_return: A return below this counts as condensing, in °C. Default 55 °C. Too high overstates the condensing share.
data_description.short_burn_min: Burns shorter than this count as short, in minutes. Default 10. Longer makes more burns short, and the verdict harsher.
data_description.monitoring_days: Days of data the monitor's verdict needs, from when the integration was added. Default 7, the shortest. It holds nothing back: control can be switched on any time, even without a verdict; until then the switch shows "not enough data".
data_description.flue_gas_warning: Flue gas above this raises a warning on a condensing boiler, in °C. Default 85 °C. Too high warns too late.
data_description.flue_gas_alarm: Flue gas above this raises an alarm, in °C. Default 100 °C. A limit set too high warns too late for plastic flue pipes.
data_description.starts_per_hour_limit: More burner starts than this in an hour raise a warning. Default 12. Too high hides short-cycling.
data_description.unstable_burns_limit: More than this many burns under a minute in a day raise a warning. Default 10. Too high hides an ignition problem.
data_description.verdict_window_days: The verdict covers this many most recent days with data. Empty (default): every day kept, up to a year, filled from the recorder at start. Never shorter than the monitoring period.

control.title: Control (experimental)
control.description: How the plugin writes to the boiler: a flow setpoint, or on and off through a relay. Until you switch control on, nothing changes; you may switch it on from the first day, even without a verdict. It then replaces VT's central boiler — remove that first and restart Home Assistant. The boiler's connection decides the path.

data_description.write_path: Asked only for an installation set up before the connection question: no control (default), a writable entity (e.g. EMS-ESP, ESPHome), the OpenTherm Gateway integration, the OTGW firmware's MQTT, or a relay for an on/off boiler. A wrong path: writes that fail or go nowhere.

control_entity.title: Writable entity
control_entity.description: The entity that takes the flow setpoint, and how control is handed back.

data.own_room_controller: The boiler has its own room controller
data.esphome_safe_start: On the ESP: safe start values and a short API reboot_timeout

data_description.setpoint_entity: A number or input_number that sets the boiler's flow temperature. Another value — the boiler's maximum, a hot-water setting — would be overwritten every 30 s or 5 min, and the water would not follow the curve.
data_description.write_type: Expiring: dropped unless repeated — repeated every 30 s. Held: the device keeps it — written on change, every 5 min and on its return; "off" included, it stays while Home Assistant is down. Persistent or unknown (default): not available — the plugin never writes to the boiler's memory, which every repeat would wear.
data_description.ch_entity: A switch that turns heating on and off — needed for control in this version: without it "off" would be a low setpoint. Turned back on at hand-back where the boiler or a thermostat takes over. Never a setting stored in the boiler's memory, nor a flag that stops heating while on (EMS-ESP's "heating off").
data_description.ch_write_type: What the device does with the switch's state. Expiring: repeated every 30 s. Held: written on change, every 5 min and on its return. Persistent or unknown: refused — the plugin never writes to the boiler's memory.
data_description.hand_back: How control returns to the boiler on every exit, after the lowest water temperature is written and the heating switch turned back on where the boiler takes over: write a value, let the device's timeout lapse (expiring writes only), or turn off an external-control switch. Required. Afterwards the boiler's or thermostat's own maximum is the only one.
data_description.hand_back_value: The setpoint written on hand-back, in °C. 0 means "own control" on some devices and "no heat" on others. Never above the highest water temperature, and never cut down to it; done once the read-back shows it.
data_description.hand_back_value_effect: What the device does with that value: its own control resumes, or heating stops. Declared "own control" where heating stops, a hand-back leaves the house unheated while the plugin says the boiler runs on its own.
data_description.hand_back_entity: The switch that enables external control: on when control starts, off on hand-back — so never a setting the device stores in its memory.
data_description.hand_back_entity_write_type: What the device does with the switch's state. Expiring: turned on again every 30 s while control holds the boiler. Held: on when control takes the boiler, every 5 min and on its return. Persistent or unknown (default): not available — every switching would wear the boiler's memory.
data_description.hand_back_timeout_min: How long, in minutes, the device keeps the last value before its own control resumes — from its documentation (1–60; default 1, as EMS-ESP's setpoint). The boiler stays at the lowest water temperature that long; the hand-back is judged after it. Too short: a false alarm; too long: a device that never lets go is reported late.
data_description.own_room_controller: Tick only if the boiler has its own room controller that asks for heat once the plugin lets go (e.g. a room unit on its EMS bus). Hand-backs then go to it, also when VT gives no answer at all. Off by default. Without such a controller, the boiler would heat on its own dial with no room in charge.
data_description.esphome_safe_start: Required for control on ESPHome; never ticked for you. The ESP keeps the last setpoint and heating until it restarts (by default after 15 min without Home Assistant), then takes its start values. Tick once those are safe unattended, restore_value is off and its reboot_timeout is a few minutes.

control_curve.title: Heating curve
control_curve.description: The flow temperature the house needs at each outdoor temperature, the lowest water temperature and the comfort correction. The water is capped by the highest water temperature of the circuits fed straight from the boiler ({circuit_max}, the circuits' forms; 70 °C where none) and the boiler's maximum heating setpoint ({boiler_max}, boiler step): the lower applies.

data.design_outdoor: Outdoor temperature at the hardest frost (curve point)

data_description.design_outdoor: The curve's design point, in °C: at this outdoor temperature the water is at the design flow temperature. Default −15 °C. Too cold a value gives too little water in frost.
data_description.design_flow: The flow temperature the heating needs at the hardest frost, in °C (e.g. from the boiler's own curve). Required, no default. Too high wastes gas and makes the burner cycle; too low leaves rooms cold. SmartPI (0.4.0) learns its own outdoor term in each zone: set the curve to what the house needs, no higher.
data_description.hard_min: The lowest water temperature the plugin sets, in °C. Default 20 °C. Too low: in mild weather the boiler stops again and again, and a non-condensing boiler condenses in its flue — take it from the manual. The plugin may suggest a value; it never changes this itself.
data_description.room: With Manual: the setpoint of the warmest room you keep, in °C. Default 20 °C. Too low leaves rooms cold in mild weather; too high raises the whole curve. With Auto, the start value until a zone is known.
data_description.exponent: How the curve bends. Empty picks it from the emitters: radiators 1.3, convectors 1.4, underfloor 1.1. The wrong bend under-heats in frost or overheats in mild weather.
data_description.offset: Shifts the whole curve up or down, in K. Default 0. Up wastes gas; down leaves rooms cold.
data_description.fallback_setpoint: Used when no outdoor temperature has been known for three hours (sensor and weather lost or suspect), in °C. Empty (default): the curve at its design point, the most heat it gives; the valves keep rooms from overheating.
data_description.comfort_correction: On (default with full control): while a zone's valve is fully open and its room stays short of its setpoint (with SmartPI learning: of the setpoint + 0.5 K), the water rises above the curve — 1 K per 30 min, at most 3 K a day, up to its limit — and falls twice as fast; not while another zone is too warm or the starts rise. What it costs: more gas, and possibly more starts. With TPI zones it can sit at its limit: in the simulation 1.75 to 5 times the starts. Watch the starts.
data_description.room_mode: Auto (default): the curve passes through the highest setpoint among the zones that heat now — at most 23 °C, following VT's presets. Manual: the value below. With Auto the warmest room sets the water for all; a room kept warm only now and then raises it too, unless left out below.
data_description.room_excluded: Zones whose setpoint Auto does not follow, e.g. a bathroom kept warmer. Such a room may stay short in mild weather; the comfort correction then raises the water for it.
data_description.comfort_correction_max_k: How far above the curve the correction may raise the water, in K. Default 3 K, 0.5 to 10; it rises at most 3 K a day. It is the only bound above the curve. Higher: more gas and warmer water for rooms that do not need it; a correction stuck at its limit means the curve is too low.

control_behaviour.title: Control behaviour
control_behaviour.description: Heating goes on and off with VT's zones, at once — after the activation delay for a start; nothing counted or timed holds it. At the advanced level: the demand thresholds and learning pauses; with full control the ramp, the decision interval and, without a heating switch, the "off" setpoint.

data_description.activation_delay_s: Seconds heating waits after the first call for heat, so slow valves open before the boiler and pump run, as VT's central boiler did; pre-filled from VT's own, for you to confirm. Stopping is never delayed. Default 0. A heating pulse shorter than the delay never starts the boiler.
data_description.ramp_k_per_min: The fastest setpoint change, in K per minute. Default 1. Faster changes stress the boiler and make zones overshoot.
data_description.decision_interval_min: How often the water temperature is decided anew, in minutes; default 5. Heating on and off follows the zones every 10 s regardless. Shorter follows the weather sooner but moves the water more often under the zones' algorithms.
data_description.off_setpoint: The setpoint written for "off" without a heating switch, in °C. Default 10, below the lowest water temperature. A low setpoint may not switch the boiler's heating off — the pump may keep running. Control without a heating switch is blocked in this version, so it is not written yet.
data_description.count_threshold: Heating is needed when at least this many zones call. Default 1, at most the number of zones. 0 leaves the power or opening threshold alone — every zone must then report what it needs, or it could never ask for heat. Higher leaves a single room without heat.
data_description.power_threshold_kw: Optional: heating is needed when the zones' mean power, as VT counts it, reaches this, in kW, while a valve is open or a device on. A zone without a device power in VT gives no data. Too high leaves small rooms without heat.
data_description.opening_threshold: Optional: heating is needed when the widest valve opening among the calling zones reaches this, in %. VT's over_climate zones give no data. Too high leaves a room that opens a little without heat.
data_description.learning_pauses: Pause SmartPI's learning while hot water runs, while control holds heating off for a boiler fault and while the water swings, so it does not learn what the boiler did; at most an hour each. Default on. Auto-TPI cannot be paused without losing what it learned: such zones are reported.

control_frost.title: Frost protection
control_frost.description: A watched zone colder than its limit starts heating, whatever else applies, where heat can reach it; heating for frost ends once every watched zone is above the release.

data_description.frost_limit: A watched zone colder than this starts heating, whatever else applies, where heat can reach it, in °C. Default 5 °C. Too low risks frozen pipes; too high heats rooms you keep off.
data_description.frost_release: Frost protection ends once every watched zone is above this, in °C. Default 7 °C, above the limit. Close to the limit, frost heating starts and stops more often.
data_description.frost_zone: Optional: watch only this zone. Empty (default): every zone. Frost heating runs only for a cold room whose valve can open; one VT keeps closed raises a repair issue. Frost heating that does not warm the room in two hours raises an alarm; it never stops.

control_alarms.title: Alarm reactions
control_alarms.description: What control does when the boiler ignores a value the plugin writes. Other alarms only inform; the plugin stops heating only while the boiler itself reports a fault that stops it. Another controller writing to the boiler always makes the plugin step aside; it never fights it.

data.return_after_outside_change: Return by itself after another controller
data.return_after_switch_hand_back: Also after the external-control switch's hand-back

data_description.write_ignored: Offered where a hand-back returns the boiler to a thermostat or its own control. Hand back: after an ignored write, control steps aside until you switch it off and on. Information (default): the plugin keeps trying and tells you. "Heating off" ignored from the start always hands back.
data_description.return_after_outside_change: Off (default): after another controller changed the boiler twice, the plugin hands back and steps aside until you switch control off and on. On: it takes the boiler back after an hour with no other writes. If the other controller only pauses, the two take turns.
data_description.return_after_switch_hand_back: Used only with the return above on. Off (default): after a hand-back through the external-control switch, control waits for you. On: it returns once the switch has read "off" for an hour — also when a person turned external control off on purpose.

control_return_confirm.title: Confirm the return by itself
control_return_confirm.description: The plugin will take the boiler back by itself an hour after another controller last wrote to it. If that controller is still there, both will control the boiler in turns. Tick to confirm.

data_description.understood: Tick to switch the return by itself on; without the tick it stays off.

confirm_blocking.title: This change stops control
confirm_blocking.description: With this change control cannot run: {first} ({more} other reasons). Saving hands the boiler back now.

data_description.save_anyway: Tick to save the change all the same. Left unticked (default), nothing is saved and the menu shows again with your changes: change them, or close the window to discard them.

control_relay.title: Relay
control_relay.description: How the plugin switches an on/off boiler, as VT's central boiler did; the boiler sets its own water temperature, so the curve and water limits do not apply. If Home Assistant stops, the relay stays as it was: switch it by hand in the relay's own app or web page. A relay in the boiler's power supply also cuts its pump overrun and frost protection; the room-thermostat terminals may carry mains voltage.

data.relay_is_separate_contact: This relay or thermostat entity is not a setting stored in the boiler's memory
data.relay_reports_state: The relay reports its real state
data.own_room_controller: The boiler has its own room controller

data_description.relay_entity: The switch on the boiler's room-thermostat terminals, or a boiler thermostat entity set to heat or off. Not a helper, not a VT zone's switch, never a setting stored in the boiler's memory. A Zigbee relay may look available long after it dies: turn availability reporting on.
data_description.relay_is_separate_contact: Tick to confirm the relay is a separate contact — or, for a boiler thermostat entity, that its heat/off mode is not stored in the boiler's memory, which every switching would wear (e.g. EMS-ESP's "heating activated"). Unsure: leave it unticked. Control does not start without it.
data_description.relay_reports_state: Yes: the plugin checks the relay's state, writes only when it differs, and steps aside if something else keeps switching it. No or I don't know (default): it repeats its command at the repeat interval, unconfirmed; a change made at the relay is undone within that time.
data_description.relay_power_on_state: What the relay does when its power returns — its own setting. Off: the boiler waits until Home Assistant gives its command. On, last state or I don't know (default): after a power cut the boiler may heat without control until Home Assistant is back.
data_description.relay_off_timer: Whether the relay switches itself off some time after "on" (Tasmota's PulseTime; a Shelly's auto-off — whether a Shelly restarts it on a repeated "on" is not documented). None: written only on a difference. A length: "on" repeated at half of it; if Home Assistant stops, the relay switches heating off by itself. I don't know (default): "on" repeated at the repeat interval; switch-offs coming the same time after "on", 9 min or more (a 10-min timer measured up to a minute short), are taken for its timer, other ones count, and the fourth within a day makes the plugin step aside — so declare its length. Set a relay timer only once the plugin's control starts.
data_description.relay_off_timer_min: The timer's length, 10–120 min, exactly as set in the relay: a switch-off at another time counts as something else switching the relay. A shorter timer is refused: each lapse would start the boiler again.
data_description.relay_repeat_s: How often the command is repeated, in seconds, 10–300; empty (default): 300 s, or VT's keep-alive where it was at most 300 s. A relay that restarted in the wrong state stays so at most this long; some relays store every command.
data_description.relay_rest_state: What the relay is set to whenever control is handed back. Off (default): without a thermostat wired to the boiler heating stops, and the plugin tells you when a room asks for heat or nears freezing. On: the boiler heats by its own setting, rooms limited only by their valves.
data_description.own_room_controller: Tick only if the boiler has its own room controller and the relay after hand-back is "on": when VT gives no answer, the relay goes on and that controller heats. With "off" the tick changes nothing. Off by default.
data_description.boiler_heats_above_w: The boiler's electric power, in W, above which it counts as heating. Empty (default): power is not used as proof. Too low: standby counts as heating; too high: real heating is missed.

control_relay_from_vt.title: Relay — moving over from Versatile Thermostat
control_relay_from_vt.description: How the plugin switches an on/off boiler, as VT's central boiler did; the boiler sets its own water temperature, so the curve and water limits do not apply. If Home Assistant stops, the relay stays as it was: switch it by hand in the relay's own app or web page. A relay in the boiler's power supply also cuts its pump overrun and frost protection; the room-thermostat terminals may carry mains voltage. VT's central boiler drives this boiler now: its relay, delay, repeat interval and thresholds are filled in where usable — check and save.
