hand_back_failed.message: Control is off, but handing the boiler back did not get through: the plugin tries again every minute. Until then the boiler may keep the last value control wrote; check its connection.

invalid_options.message: The configuration cannot be used ({subject}): {reason} Open the options and correct it.

blocked_no_write_path.message: Control is not set up: choose in the options how the plugin writes to the boiler. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_no_setpoint_entity.message: Pick the entity that takes the flow setpoint. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_write_type_not_supported.message: The setpoint entity is declared persistent or of unknown write type, and the plugin never writes to the boiler's persistent memory: declare it expiring or held in the options. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_no_hand_back.message: Choose how control is handed back to the boiler: a value, the device's own timeout or a switch. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_no_gateway.message: Pick the OpenTherm Gateway under "Boiler interface". Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_no_mqtt_topic.message: Enter the gateway's MQTT topic prefix and node name under "Boiler interface". Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_mqtt_topic_invalid.message: Enter the gateway's MQTT topic prefix and node name as its firmware uses them, without spaces or the wildcards + and #. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_no_confirmed_setpoint.message: Map the setpoint the boiler received (the read-back) in Boiler signals. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_thermostat_setpoint_same_as_read.message: The thermostat's own setpoint and the setpoint read-back are one entity: the read-back shows the plugin's value, not the thermostat's request. Pick the thermostat's own entity in Boiler interface, or the boiler's setpoint in Boiler signals. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_no_topology.message: Declare how the gateway is connected. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_curve_not_entered.message: Enter the heating curve, at least the design flow temperature. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_one_direct_circuit_only.message: This version controls at most one circuit fed straight from the boiler, with circuits behind a fixed thermostatic mixing valve or run by other automation — not a second straight circuit, nor one the boiler mixes (CH2). Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_underfloor_without_max_flow.message: Underfloor heating on an unmixed circuit needs a maximum flow temperature for that circuit. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_count_threshold_above_zones.message: The demand threshold asks for more zones than are configured, so heating would never be asked for: lower it in the options. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_no_zones.message: Control needs at least one Versatile Thermostat zone: add them in the options. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_ha_starting.message: Home Assistant is still starting. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_vt_central_boiler_active.message: Versatile Thermostat's own central boiler is configured, or may have run since Home Assistant started: untick it, so only one controller drives the boiler, and restart Home Assistant. Control waits until Home Assistant has restarted, even once you have unticked it — also when VT's central configuration was created or changed after Home Assistant started, even without a central boiler. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_vt_central_boiler_unknown.message: Versatile Thermostat's central boiler cannot be ruled out yet: VT's central configuration failed to load (see Settings → Devices & services), or its settings do not say whether its central boiler is on. Control waits for it. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_control_error.message: Control stopped after an internal error. Check the log, then switch control off and on again. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_monitor_failed.message: The plugin's monitor has failed for 5 minutes, so control handed the boiler back; it resumes on its own once the monitor works again. Check the log. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_control_state_not_saved.message: The plugin cannot save its memory of the boiler (see the repair issue), so control does not take the boiler; it resumes on its own once saving has worked again for a few minutes. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_timeout_needs_expiring_writes.message: The device's timeout hands back only with expiring writes: choose a hand-back value or a switch in the options. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_setpoint_outside_entity_range.message: The setpoint entity does not accept every value control may write (a limit, the "off" setpoint or the hand-back value): adjust them to its range in the options. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_off_setpoint_not_below_hard_min.message: The "off" setpoint is not at least 1 °C below the lowest water temperature: lower it in the options. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_setpoint_unit_not_supported.message: The setpoint entity's unit is not a temperature unit (°C, °F or K), so a value written would mean something else to it: pick the boiler's flow setpoint entity in the options. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_hand_back_switch_not_writable.message: Declare the external control switch expiring or held: the plugin never writes to the boiler's persistent memory. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_hand_back_value_above_max.message: The hand-back value is above the highest water temperature or the circuit's maximum: the boiler would get hotter water than the circuit allows. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_off_setpoint_near_hand_back_valu.message: "Off" is within 0.5 K of the hand-back value, which returns the boiler to its own control: "off" would hand the boiler back instead of stopping heating. Pick another value. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

monitor_refresh_failed.message: The plugin's monitor could not compute its data; the log has the details.

blocked_setpoint_step_too_coarse.message: The setpoint entity now takes values in steps above 1 °C, so its read-back cannot confirm a value: pick another entity in the options. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_heating_off_ignored.message: From the start of the session the boiler did not take "heating off" — or the relay its "off" — so control stopped and handed the boiler back. Check the heating switch or relay and the boiler's settings, then switch control off and on. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_heating_on_ignored.message: From the start of the session the boiler did not take "heating on" — or the relay its "on" — so control stopped and handed the boiler back. Check the heating switch or relay, the entity that confirms it and the boiler's settings, then switch control off and on. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_relay_off_not_taken.message: The relay took commands earlier, then did not show "off" for about 15 minutes, so control stopped — the boiler may keep heating; the relay was set once to its state after hand-back. Check the relay, its link and the entity, then switch control off and on. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_hand_back_switch_is_heating_swit.message: The external control switch is also the heating switch or the setpoint entity: handing back would switch it on and off for ever. Pick another entity in the options. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_entity_for_two_signals.message: One entity feeds two signals, so the later one is not used. Pick another entity for it in the signals options. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_topology_not_for_path.message: The gateway connection does not suit the write path: choose another under "Boiler interface". Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_no_heating_switch.message: Control needs a heating switch the boiler does not store in its memory: without one, "off" would be a low setpoint, and whether that stops the boiler and its pump is not known yet (EMS-ESP's own setpoint 0 aside). Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_gateway_not_set_up.message: The OpenTherm Gateway integration of the gateway picked is removed or disabled: the commands would go nowhere. Set it up or enable it, or pick another gateway in the options. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_mqtt_not_set_up.message: The MQTT integration is removed or disabled: the commands would go nowhere. Set it up or enable it. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_zone_not_vt.message: A zone is not a Versatile Thermostat thermostat, and only those can be zones: remove it in the options. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_zone_on_boiler_thermostat.message: A Versatile Thermostat zone is built on the boiler's or gateway's own thermostat entity: it would ask for heat whenever the flame burns. Build the zone on a room sensor and its valves or radiator thermostats instead. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_design_flow_too_low.message: The design flow temperature must be at least 5 K above the curve's room temperature. Correct it in the options. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_design_flow_above_hard_max.message: The design flow temperature is above the highest water temperature, so the curve would be cut off in frost. Raise the highest water temperature or lower the design flow in the options. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_design_outdoor_too_warm.message: The outdoor temperature at the hardest frost must be at least 10 K below the curve's room temperature. Correct it in the options. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_hard_min_not_below_design_flow.message: The lowest water temperature must be below the design flow temperature. Correct it in the options. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_hard_min_above_max.message: The lowest water temperature is above the circuit's or the boiler's maximum: the hand-back would first send the boiler hotter water than they allow. Lower it in the options. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_thermostat_on_off.message: An on/off contact is wired to the gateway's thermostat terminals: the gateway's "heating off" would block it after a Home Assistant crash, so control is not offered. The monitor keeps running. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_thermostat_kind_unknown.message: Control waits until you say, under "Boiler interface", what is wired to the gateway's thermostat terminals. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_thermostat_kind_dont_know.message: Control waits: "Boiler interface" says "I don't know" about what is wired to the gateway's thermostat terminals. Check the wiring and give the answer there. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_thermostat_kind_contradicts_topo.message: This answer does not fit the gateway connection: an OpenTherm thermostat means "Gateway with a thermostat", nothing means stand-alone. Pick the other connection. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_boiler_class_no_control.message: The plugin cannot write to this boiler: it is read through an integration that only reads, or the boiler's own module with monitoring chosen. Check "Connection and boiler type" and "Control mode". Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_path_not_for_boiler_class.message: The write path does not suit the boiler: a relay for an on/off boiler, a setpoint path for one that takes a water temperature. Check how the boiler is connected under "Connection and boiler type". Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_no_relay_entity.message: Pick the relay in the control options. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_relay_contact_not_confirmed.message: Control waits until you confirm, in the relay options, that the relay is a separate contact and not a setting stored in the boiler's memory. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_relay_domain_not_supported.message: The relay must be a switch or a boiler thermostat entity, not a helper. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_relay_climate_modes.message: This thermostat entity cannot be set to both heat and off. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_relay_used_by_zone.message: A Versatile Thermostat zone already switches this entity. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_entity_used_by_zone.message: A Versatile Thermostat zone drives the setpoint entity, the heating switch or the external-control switch: pick entities the zones do not drive. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_relay_of_boiler_interface.message: This entity belongs to the boiler's or VT's own integration, not to a relay. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_relay_in_another_role.message: The relay is an entity the options already use in another role or as a signal. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_no_flame_signal.message: Water-temperature control needs the flame mapped in the signals. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_no_flow_signal.message: Water-temperature control needs the flow temperature mapped in the signals. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_control_mode_monitor.message: Monitoring only is chosen under "Control mode": the plugin writes nothing to the boiler. Choose a control mode there to set up control. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_connection_not_for_path.message: The control set up writes through another path than the boiler's connection now: answer the control items again for the connection chosen under "Connection and boiler type". Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_topology_not_for_connection.message: ESPHome OpenTherm and EMS-ESP are controllers on Home Assistant's side: the topology under "Boiler interface" must be virtual. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_esphome_start_not_confirmed.message: Not confirmed that the ESP starts at safe values with a short API reboot_timeout: it would keep the last setpoint and heating for up to 15 minutes if Home Assistant stopped. Tick it in Control device once the ESP is set so. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

auto_tpi_blocked.title: Auto-TPI cannot learn in some zones
auto_tpi_blocked.description: These zones run Auto-TPI and are marked "used by the central boiler" in VT, but VT's central boiler is off — the plugin replaces it — so Auto-TPI skips learning in them: {zones}. Clearing that mark lets it learn — but also while hot water charges or the water swings, and while zones call and the boiler does not heat (after a hand-back, at a fault, during the activation delay and the monitoring period), which can skew it: the plugin cannot pause Auto-TPI.

hand_back_owed.title: Handing the boiler back has not got through

confirm.title: Handing the boiler back has not got through
confirm.description:
The plugin cannot hand the boiler back: its setpoint entity, heating switch or gateway does not take it. It retries every minute; until it gets through, the boiler may keep the last value the plugin wrote. Check that the device is available.

If you have returned the boiler to its own control by hand — or the device is gone for good — confirm here: the plugin stops retrying and forgets what it owed, and the options accept another device. Confirm only once the boiler really runs on its own.

abort.entry_busy: The integration is being set up or reloaded just now, so nothing was changed. Wait a moment and confirm again.

control_options_invalid.title: The control options cannot be used
control_options_invalid.description: The saved control options cannot be used, so control is off; the monitor keeps running. The log names the option; open the options and set control up again.

control_state_unreadable.title: The plugin's memory of the boiler could not be read
control_state_unreadable.description: The file where the plugin remembers whether it holds the boiler is missing or damaged. To be safe it hands the boiler back first, where its options let it; this notice goes once the boiler shows that hand-back. Control then works as usual. While it stays, check the boiler and the control switch.

setup_failed_not_heated.title: The plugin did not start: the house is not heated
setup_failed_not_heated.description: The plugin could not start, and here a hand-back stops heating (a gateway without a thermostat, a hand-back value that stops heating, or a relay resting "off"): the house is not heated unless something else heats it. In Settings → Devices & services, read the entry's error, fix it and reload the entry.

setup_failed_may_not_be_heated.title: The plugin did not start: the house may not be heated
setup_failed_may_not_be_heated.description: The plugin could not start, and its options cannot be read, so it cannot tell what the boiler does without it: where a hand-back stops heating, the house is not heated. In Settings → Devices & services, read the entry's error, fix it and reload the entry.

control_state_not_saved.title: The plugin cannot save its memory of the boiler
control_state_not_saved.description: Saving the plugin's memory of the boiler failed (a full disk or a read-only storage; the log has the error), so control does not take the boiler: a restart could forget what it wrote. Where a hand-back stops heating, the boiler does not heat meanwhile. The plugin tries again every minute; control resumes on its own once saving has worked for {minutes} minutes. Check Home Assistant's storage.

hand_back_owed_after_removal.title: The boiler may still hold a value from Smart Boiler for Versatile Thermostat
hand_back_owed_after_removal.description: The integration was removed before its hand-back reached the boiler. Return the boiler to its own control by hand — reset the setpoint entity, or clear the gateway's overrides — and then ignore this issue.

learning_left_off_after_removal.title: SmartPI's learning may still be off in some zones
learning_left_off_after_removal.description: The integration was removed while control had paused SmartPI's learning in these zones, and it could not be seen switched back on: {zones}. SmartPI keeps learning off until it is switched on — in SmartPI's own settings, or with its service "set_smartpi_learning". Switch it on there, and then ignore this issue.

learning_not_paused.title: The plugin cannot pause learning in some zones
learning_not_paused.description: Control cannot pause learning in these zones during hot water and water swings: {zones}. Auto-TPI could only be paused by wiping what it learned; a SmartPI without a learning flag cannot be paused. They keep learning through those moments, which can skew what they learn.

vt_feature_manager_unsupported.title: VT's thermostats cannot show the plugin's zone value
vt_feature_manager_unsupported.description: The Versatile Thermostat installed here cannot load the plugin's feature manager (feature managers need VT {version} or newer, with vtherm_api 0.5 or newer; the plugin is tested with VT 10.4.0), so its thermostats cannot show whether heat reaches their zones. Update Versatile Thermostat to show it.

vt_reload_needed.title: Some VT thermostats need a reload to show the plugin's value
vt_reload_needed.description: These thermostats were already running when the plugin registered with Versatile Thermostat, and pick it up only when VT reloads: {zones}. Reload Versatile Thermostat to show on them whether heat reaches their zones. Nothing else depends on it.

vt_central_entry_not_running.title: Versatile Thermostat's central configuration is not running
vt_central_entry_not_running.description: Its setup failed, and its settings say VT's central boiler is on. Control waits, so that two controllers never drive the boiler: fix VT's central configuration, or untick its central boiler and restart Home Assistant.

entity_removed.title: An entity the plugin uses is gone
entity_removed.description: {field}: {entity} is no longer in Home Assistant. Pick another one in the options; until then the plugin works without it.

hand_back_taken_by_other.title: After the hand-back another controller holds the boiler
hand_back_taken_by_other.description: After the hand-back another controller — an automation, a device's program, another integration — holds what the plugin had set: {target}. The hand-back counts as done; the plugin does not write there again. Where a hand-back stops heating, the boiler heats only under that controller. If you expect none, find it.

monitor_failed.title: Control handed the boiler back: the plugin's monitor keeps failing
monitor_failed.description: The plugin's monitor has failed for 5 minutes — an error in the plugin; the log has the details — so control handed the boiler back. It resumes by itself once the monitor works again. Meanwhile a thermostat or the boiler's own control heats where your installation has one; where a hand-back stops heating, the boiler does not heat until control resumes.

monitor_recovered.title: The plugin's monitor failed for a while; control has resumed
monitor_recovered.description: The plugin's monitor failed from {since} to {until}, so control handed the boiler back meanwhile. The monitor works again and control has resumed by itself. The log has the error; if this happens again, report it.

control_stopped_heating.title: Control stopped and the boiler does not heat
control_stopped_heating.description: Control handed the boiler back because something now blocks it (the control switch lists what). With this installation a hand-back stops heating: the boiler heats again when control resumes once the blocker is gone, or when you return it to its own control. Frost protection now rests on the boiler's own, if it has one.

control_latched.title: Control stepped aside: another controller writes to the boiler
control_latched.description: Another controller changed what the plugin writes again after the plugin wrote it back once — {value} on {target} — so the plugin stepped aside and handed the boiler back. With a thermostat or the boiler's own control it keeps heating; without one, only under that controller. Stop it, then switch control off and on; with "Return by itself" on, control also returns after an hour without other writes.

control_latched_switch.title: Control stepped aside: another controller switches the boiler
control_latched_switch.description: Another controller switched {target}, which the plugin had not done, so the plugin stepped aside and handed the boiler back. With a thermostat or the boiler's own control it keeps heating; without one, only under that controller. Stop it, then switch control off and on; with "Return by itself" on, control also returns after an hour without other writes.

control_latched_heating_off_ignored.title: Control stopped: the boiler does not take "heating off"
control_latched_heating_off_ignored.description: From the start of the session the boiler did not take "heating off", so the plugin handed it back. Where a hand-back stops heating, the boiler does not heat until control resumes. Check the heating switch picked in the options and the boiler's settings, then switch control off and on.

control_latched_heating_on_ignored.title: Control stopped: the boiler does not take "heating on"
control_latched_heating_on_ignored.description: From the start of the session the boiler did not take "heating on" — or its confirming entity never showed it — so the plugin handed it back. Until control resumes it does not heat the house, frost protection included. Check the heating switch, its confirming entity (not a status of whether the boiler heats now) and the boiler's settings, then switch control off and on.

control_latched_write_ignored.title: Control handed back: the boiler ignores a value the plugin writes
control_latched_write_ignored.description: The boiler did not take a value the plugin wrote (the alarm "Control: the boiler does not accept a command" names it), and "Boiler ignores a value" is set to hand back, so control handed the boiler back; the thermostat or its own control heats now. Check the entity and the boiler's settings, then switch control off and on.

control_latched_other.title: Control stays handed back after an earlier alarm
control_latched_other.description: An earlier version handed the boiler back for an alarm that now only informs ({alarm}); control stays handed back until you switch it off and on. Where a hand-back stops heating, the boiler does not heat meanwhile.

hand_back_boiler_link_lost.title: Control handed the boiler back: its data is lost
hand_back_boiler_link_lost.description: The boiler's flame or flow was not fresh for 5 minutes within 10, so control handed the boiler back — nothing is written without fresh data. Where a hand-back stops heating, the boiler does not heat meanwhile. Control resumes once the data is fresh for a minute. Check the device, its link and the flame and flow entities.

hand_back_control_error.title: Control stopped after an internal error
hand_back_control_error.description: An error in the plugin stopped control, and it handed the boiler back (the log has the details). Where a hand-back stops heating, the boiler does not heat meanwhile. Control stays stopped until you switch it off and on; if the error comes back, report it with the log.

no_zone_known_off.title: Versatile Thermostat gives no answer: the boiler is not heating
no_zone_known_off.description: None of the zones answers ({zones}), so nothing can ask for heat. The plugin keeps the boiler's heating off and resumes as soon as a zone answers. Check that Versatile Thermostat is loaded, its thermostats are enabled and their entity IDs are the ones in the plugin's options.

no_zone_known_handed_back.title: Versatile Thermostat gives no answer: the boiler is back on its thermostat or its own room controller
no_zone_known_handed_back.description: None of the zones answers ({zones}), so nothing can ask for heat. The plugin handed the boiler back to the thermostat on the gateway, or to the boiler's own room controller, and takes it again as soon as a zone answers. Check that Versatile Thermostat is loaded, its thermostats are enabled and their entity IDs are the ones in the plugin's options.

no_zone_known_monitor.title: Versatile Thermostat gives no answer
no_zone_known_monitor.description: None of the zones answers ({zones}); the monitor cannot judge them. Check that Versatile Thermostat is loaded, its thermostats are enabled and their entity IDs are the ones in the plugin's options.

no_criterion_judged_off.title: No demand criterion can be judged: the boiler is not heating
no_criterion_judged_off.description: The zones answer, but no demand criterion set in the options gets data from them, so no call for heat can be seen ({criteria}: "power" needs a device power in VT, "opening" a valve opening or duty cycle). The plugin keeps heating off until a criterion has data. Set the device power in VT, or a zone count of 1 or more in the control options.

no_criterion_judged_handed_back.title: No demand criterion can be judged: the boiler is back on its thermostat or its own room controller
no_criterion_judged_handed_back.description: The zones answer, but no demand criterion set in the options gets data from them, so no call for heat can be seen ({criteria}: "power" needs a device power in VT, "opening" a valve opening or duty cycle). The plugin handed the boiler back to the thermostat or its own room controller, and takes it again once a criterion has data. Set the device power in VT, or a zone count of 1 or more in the control options.

no_criterion_judged_monitor.title: No demand criterion can be judged
no_criterion_judged_monitor.description: The zones answer, but no demand criterion set in the options gets data from them, so no call for heat can be seen ({criteria}: "power" needs a device power in VT, "opening" a valve opening or duty cycle). Switched on, control could not heat for any room. Set the device power in VT, or a zone count of 1 or more in the control options.

frost_zone_closed.title: A room below the frost limit cannot get heat
frost_zone_closed.description: {zones}: Versatile Thermostat keeps the valve closed (the thermostat is off, or its target is below the frost limit), so the plugin cannot heat it and does not start the boiler for it. Use VT's frost preset instead of off; VT's central frost mode needs a frost temperature set in every thermostat.

frost_zone_closed_window.title: A room below the frost limit cannot get heat: window open
frost_zone_closed_window.description: {zones}: Versatile Thermostat keeps the valve closed because it detects an open window, so the plugin cannot heat it and does not start the boiler for it. The room stays unheated until VT opens it again: close the window, or check VT's window detection for that room.

frost_zone_closed_central_mode.title: A room below the frost limit cannot get heat: VT's central mode
frost_zone_closed_central_mode.description: {zones}: Versatile Thermostat keeps the valve closed because of its central mode, so the plugin cannot heat it and does not start the boiler for it. With the central mode "Stopped" the room stays unheated until VT opens it again; VT's central frost mode needs a frost temperature set in every thermostat. The plugin never changes VT's mode.

frost_zone_closed_vt_function.title: A room below the frost limit cannot get heat: a VT function keeps it off
frost_zone_closed_vt_function.description: {zones}: one of Versatile Thermostat's own functions (its safety mode, or auto start/stop) keeps the valve closed, so the plugin cannot heat it and does not start the boiler for it. The room stays unheated until VT opens it again: check that thermostat's room sensor and its auto start/stop settings.

frost_zone_closed_mixed.title: Rooms below the frost limit cannot get heat
frost_zone_closed_mixed.description: {zones}: VT keeps their valves closed for different reasons, so the plugin cannot heat them. For a thermostat that is off, use VT's frost preset instead; a room closed for a window, VT's "Stopped" or another VT function stays unheated until VT opens it.

thermostat_kind_missing.title: Say what is wired to the gateway's thermostat terminals
thermostat_kind_missing.description: Control of the boiler waits for the answer to a question under "Boiler interface": what is wired to the gateway's thermostat terminals. Without a thermostat (stand-alone) the boiler does not heat meanwhile.

wall_thermostat_fallback.title: The wall thermostat would keep the house cool after a hand-back
wall_thermostat_fallback.description: The wall thermostat on the gateway is set to {value} °C. After a hand-back, or while Home Assistant is down, it heats the house by this setting and its own program. Set it to what the house should get.

wall_thermostat_fallback_unknown.title: The wall thermostat reports no setpoint
wall_thermostat_fallback_unknown.description: The wall thermostat on the gateway reports no setpoint. After a hand-back, or while Home Assistant is down, it heats the house by its own setting and program. Check that they are what the house should get, and that the wall thermostat's setpoint picked among the signals reports.

lowest_water_suggestion.title: The boiler keeps stopping at the lowest water temperature
lowest_water_suggestion.description: In the last {days} days, {short} of {burns} heating burns at about {reference} °C were shorter than {limit} min and ended because the water was warm enough, while rooms still asked for heat. Consider raising the lowest water temperature to about {value} °C in the control options. Longer burns are likely; fewer starts are not guaranteed. Nothing changes until you do.

lowest_water_suggestion_boiler.title: The boiler keeps stopping at its lowest water temperature
lowest_water_suggestion_boiler.description: In the last {days} days, {short} of {burns} heating burns at about {reference} °C were shorter than {limit} min and ended because the water was warm enough, while rooms still asked for heat. Raising the minimum flow temperature (or the curve's foot point) of the device that sets your water to about {value} °C lengthens burns; the plugin changes nothing there.

read_back_waiting.title: Control waits for the gateway's confirmation
read_back_waiting.description: Control is on, but the setpoint read-back (in Boiler signals, the heating setpoint the boiler received) has shown no value for 5 minutes, so the plugin does not take the boiler: it could never see a hand-back get through. Where a hand-back stops heating, the boiler does not heat meanwhile. Check the gateway and that entity (its "Control setpoint 1").

write_ignored_no_heat.title: The boiler does not accept the command: the house is not heated
write_ignored_no_heat.description: From the start of the session the boiler has not taken the water temperature the plugin writes (the alarm "Control: the boiler does not accept a command" names it), and here nothing else heats: the house is not heated, frost protection included. The plugin keeps control and tries again at the next session — when you switch control off and on, or after a restart. Check the boiler's settings and the entities picked.

setpoint_not_shown.title: The boiler does not show the plugin's water temperature
setpoint_not_shown.description: For 5 minutes the setpoint read-back has shown another water temperature than the plugin's. The plugin keeps control and does not hand the boiler back for this: the boiler may keep its own value (a limit, a lock), or the read-back may be late or wrong. Check the boiler's maximum and the heating setpoint mapped in Boiler signals.

no_sign_boiler_heats.title: No sign the boiler heats
no_sign_boiler_heats.description: For {minutes} minutes heating has been on while a room asks for heat, and the boiler has shown no sign of heating (no flame, or no rise in flow) with the water below the setpoint. It may be locked out after a fault, in summer mode, switched off on its panel or in the maker's app, or without gas: check its display and its gas. Control goes on and does not hand the boiler back for this.

relay_unreachable_off.title: The relay cannot be reached
relay_unreachable_off.description: {relay} has been out of reach for 5 minutes. The plugin cannot switch the boiler and sends its command again as soon as the relay returns; you can switch it by hand in its own app or page. Until then it stays as it was, or does what its own settings say: after a power cut it starts off, as you declared, so the boiler waits off.

relay_unreachable_on.title: The relay cannot be reached
relay_unreachable_on.description: {relay} has been out of reach for 5 minutes. The plugin cannot switch the boiler and sends its command again as soon as the relay returns; you can switch it by hand in its own app or page. Until then it stays as it was, or does what its own settings say: after a power cut it starts on, as you declared, so the boiler may heat without control.

relay_unreachable_last.title: The relay cannot be reached
relay_unreachable_last.description: {relay} has been out of reach for 5 minutes. The plugin cannot switch the boiler and sends its command again as soon as the relay returns; you can switch it by hand in its own app or page. Until then it stays as it was, or does what its own settings say: after a power cut it returns to its last state, as you declared, so the boiler may heat without control.

relay_unreachable_unknown.title: The relay cannot be reached
relay_unreachable_unknown.description: {relay} has been out of reach for 5 minutes. The plugin cannot switch the boiler and sends its command again as soon as the relay returns; you can switch it by hand in its own app or page. Until then it stays as it was, or does what its own settings say: what it does after a power cut is not known, so the boiler may heat without control.

relay_ignored.title: The relay does not accept the command — check it
relay_ignored.description: {relay} did not take the plugin's command after three tries this session. Nothing else controls the boiler now: check the relay and the entity picked in the options. The plugin tries again when control next takes the boiler. Control stays stopped until you switch it off and on.

relay_ignored_off.title: The relay does not accept the command — check it
relay_ignored_off.description: {relay} did not take the plugin's command after three tries this session. Nothing else controls the boiler now: check the relay and the entity picked in the options. The plugin tries again when control next takes the boiler. The boiler may keep heating: the relay does not switch off. Control stays stopped until you switch it off and on.

relay_not_taking.title: The relay has stopped taking commands: the house is not heated
relay_not_taking.description: {relay} took the plugin's commands earlier, but for about 15 minutes — three checks — it has shown none of them, and it does not show "on" now: the boiler gets no heat demand, so the house is not heated, frost protection included. The plugin sends "on" again at every check. Check the relay, its link and the entity picked.

relay_not_taking_off.title: The relay has stopped taking commands: the boiler may keep heating
relay_not_taking_off.description: {relay} took the plugin's commands earlier, but for about 15 minutes — three checks — it has shown none of them, and it does not show "off" now: the boiler may keep heating, as the relay does not switch off. Control stopped; the relay was set once to its state after hand-back, which cannot be relied on either. Check the relay, its link and the entity, then switch control off and on.

relay_rests_off.title: The boiler does not heat while control is off
relay_rests_off.description: Control of the boiler is off and the relay rests off, while {zones} ask for heat or are near freezing. The boiler now heats only through a thermostat wired to it, if there is one; you can also switch the relay by hand in its own app or page. Switch control on again, or change the relay's state after hand-back in the options.

relay_timer_seen.title: The relay keeps switching off a fixed time after "on"
relay_timer_seen.description: {relay} keeps switching off about {minutes} min after "on" (or a whole multiple of it) while its timer is "I don't know" — the relay's own timer, or an automation such as a "maximum run time", which looks the same. The plugin switches it on again at once, no longer counts these, and repeats "on" at least every half of that time. If it is the relay's timer, read its length in the relay's own settings and declare it; if an automation, change it.

control_latched_relay_off.title: Control stepped aside: something else switches the relay
control_latched_relay_off.description: Something else keeps switching {relay} — an automation, its button, a person, or restarts it does not report — so the plugin stepped aside: it switched the relay off once, its state after hand-back, and leaves it alone. Without a thermostat wired to the boiler, heating stops. Declare the relay's state after a power cut and its timer in the options, then switch control off and on.

control_latched_relay_on.title: Control stepped aside: something else switches the relay
control_latched_relay_on.description: Something else keeps switching {relay} — an automation, its button, a person, or restarts it does not report — so the plugin stepped aside: it switched the relay on once, its state after hand-back, and leaves it alone: the boiler heats by its own setting, without room control. Declare the relay's state after a power cut and its timer in the options, then switch control off and on.

control_latched_relay_short_timer_off.title: Control stepped aside: the relay switches itself off every few minutes
control_latched_relay_short_timer_off.description: {relay} switched itself off about every {minutes} min after "on" — its own timer (auto-off, "inching") or an automation. A timer that short starts the boiler again each time, so at the fourth within a day the plugin stepped aside: the relay is off, its state after hand-back. Without a thermostat wired to the boiler, heating stops. Set the relay's timer to at least 30 min, or switch the timer off, and declare it — or change the automation; then switch control off and on.

control_latched_relay_short_timer_on.title: Control stepped aside: the relay switches itself off every few minutes
control_latched_relay_short_timer_on.description: {relay} switched itself off about every {minutes} min after "on" — its own timer (auto-off, "inching") or an automation. A timer that short starts the boiler again each time, so at the fourth within a day the plugin stepped aside: it switched the relay on, its state after hand-back — but its timer switches it off again within minutes, so the boiler may not heat at all. Set the relay's timer to at least 30 min, or switch the timer off, and declare it — or change the automation; then switch control off and on.

control_latched_relay_heating_off_ignore.title: Control stopped: the relay does not take "off"
control_latched_relay_heating_off_ignore.description: From the start of the session {relay} did not take the plugin's "off": the boiler may keep heating, as the relay does not switch off. Control stopped; the relay was set once to its state after hand-back, which cannot be relied on either. Check the relay and the entity picked in the options, then switch control off and on. The monitor keeps running.

control_latched_relay_heating_on_ignored.title: Control stopped: the relay does not take "on"
control_latched_relay_heating_on_ignored.description: From the start of the session {relay} did not take the plugin's "on": the boiler gets no heat demand from the plugin, so the house is not heated, frost protection included. Control stopped; the relay was set once to its state after hand-back, which cannot be relied on either. Check the relay and the entity picked in the options, then switch control off and on. The monitor keeps running.

control_latched_relay_off_not_taken.title: Control stopped: the relay stopped taking "off"
control_latched_relay_off_not_taken.description: {relay} took the plugin's commands earlier in this session, then did not show "off" for about 15 minutes: the boiler may keep heating, as the relay does not switch off. Control stopped; the relay was set once to its state after hand-back, which cannot be relied on either. Check the relay, its connection and the entity picked in the options, then switch control off and on. The monitor keeps running.

add_water.title: Heating water pressure is low — add water
add_water.description: The pressure is {value} bar, below the {threshold} bar you set from the boiler's manual. Add water with the filling tap as the manual describes, watching the boiler's gauge, then close the tap. If it keeps falling, look for a leak. Heating carries on; the boiler stops by itself if the pressure falls too far.

pressure_high.title: Heating water pressure is high
pressure_high.description: The pressure is {value} bar, above your alarm limit of {limit} bar (keep it below the safety valve's rating, printed on the valve). Check that the filling tap is closed; to lower it, let the system cool and let a little water out at a radiator's bleed valve until the gauge shows the cold pressure from the manual. A pressure that jumps when heating runs points to the expansion vessel. Heating carries on.

flue_gas_high.title: Flue gas too hot
flue_gas_high.description: The flue gas is {value} °C, above your alarm limit of {limit} °C. Book a boiler service: heat exchanger, flue and condensate pipe, water circulation. The boiler's own flue protection may turn it down or lock it out. Heating carries on.

pressure_falling.title: Heating water pressure keeps falling
pressure_falling.description: Your pressure keeps falling — there is a risk of a leak. Over the last days it fell by {change} bar, with the water temperature taken into account. Look for drips at radiators, valves and the boiler, and at the safety valve's outlet; if you find none, have the system checked.

boiler_fault.title: The boiler reports a fault that stops it
boiler_fault.description: The boiler reports a fault that stops it ({entity}). The plugin keeps heating off while it does and switches it on again when the boiler clears it. Read the fault on the boiler and follow its manual.

reactions_removed.title: Alarm reactions no longer offered
reactions_removed.description: These alarm reactions are no longer offered and now only inform: {alarms}. The plugin stops heating only while the boiler itself reports a fault that stops it; the other alarms tell you what to do.

installation_empty_circuit.title: A heating circuit has no rooms
installation_empty_circuit.description: No Versatile Thermostat zone is assigned to these circuits: {circuits}. The plugin cannot tell when they need heat, and shows no critical room for them. Add their rooms in the integration's options, or remove the circuits.

installation_underfloor_without_max_flow.title: Underfloor heating without a water limit
installation_underfloor_without_max_flow.description: These circuits feed underfloor heating straight from the boiler, without a mixing valve, and have no maximum flow temperature: {circuits}. Water that is too hot can damage a floor. Enter each circuit's maximum flow temperature — the floor's limit from its installer or manual — in the integration's options; until then control stays blocked.

learning_not_resumed.title: The plugin could not switch learning back on in some zones
learning_not_resumed.description: Control paused SmartPI's learning in these zones and has not been able to switch it back on for a day, so it no longer tries: {zones}. SmartPI keeps learning off until it is switched on — in SmartPI's own settings, or with its service "set_smartpi_learning". If you switched it off yourself, nothing needs doing. This notice goes once learning is on again.

esphome_no_repeats.title: ESPHome sensors do not repeat unchanged values
esphome_no_repeats.description: {entity} did not report an unchanged value again in six hours: Home Assistant writes an ESPHome sensor only on a change, unless the ESP sends it with force_update: true. Without it a steady value cannot be told from a frozen one, and these sensors are judged by availability alone. Add force_update: true to them in the ESP's configuration.

curve_too_low.title: The heating curve looks too low for {zones}
curve_too_low.description: For three hours the comfort correction has been at its limit of {limit} K, and most rooms — {zones} — still do not reach their setpoints with valves fully open. Possible causes, the likeliest first: the heating curve is too low (its design flow, in Heating curve); a room's radiator too small for it; a room losing heat (a window, leaks). The correction holds at its limit and does not climb further.

room_short_at_limit.title: {zones} stays short of its setpoint
room_short_at_limit.description: For three hours the comfort correction has been at its limit of {limit} K, and {zones} still does not reach its setpoint with its valve fully open, while the other rooms do. Possible causes, the likeliest first: its radiator is too small for it; it loses heat (a window, its valve, leaks); the heating curve is too low for it. The correction holds at its limit and does not climb further.

boiler_power_limit.title: The boiler is at its power limit for {zones}
boiler_power_limit.description: For three hours the burner has run without a break while {zones} stays short, and the water stays over a kelvin below the setpoint at 90 % modulation or more: the boiler cannot give more. Check that it is set to its full heating power, and whether the house loses more heat than the boiler was sized for. Control changes nothing.
